## MiniMax H3

[MiniMax H3](https://www.minimax.io/blog/minimax-h3) is MiniMax's general-purpose, omni-modal generation model. It jointly understands text, image, video, and audio, and generates video with **native stereo audio**: voice, sound effects, and music are modeled jointly in a single forward pass, not layered on afterward. Output is up to 2K resolution, 24fps, and up to about 15 seconds.

## ComfyUI links
- [ComfyUI#15224](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI/pull/15224)
- [🤗 Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3)

## About this workflow

This template runs the **reference-to-video (ref2va)** task using the `MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo` node. It takes any mix of reference images, videos, and standalone audio, and weaves them into the generation to lock in a character's identity, a style, a motion, a camera move, or a voice.

**Key inputs**

- **ref_images / ref_videos / ref_video_audios / ref_audios**: up to 9 reference images, 3 reference videos (each may carry its own paired soundtrack), and 3 standalone reference audio clips
- **prompt**: reference the inputs by tag, in the exact order they were connected, for example `<Picture 1>`, `<Video 1>`, `<Audio 1>`, then describe the target scene, motion, and audio
- **ref_image_size**: `match` scales references down to the generation's resolution (faster); `max` keeps up to a 2048px short edge for stronger identity fidelity, at the cost of speed since reference tokens ride along every sampling step
- **width / height**: set via Resolution Selector.
- **duration (seconds)**: converted to a valid frame `length` by the Math Expression node

**Sampling and decode**

- Sampler: `res_multistep`. `beta` or `normal` scheduler tends to outperform `simple` for reference-heavy prompts like this one
- The sampler's joint audio+video `LATENT` output feeds directly into both `VAEDecode` (video, `minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16`) and `VAEDecodeAudio` (audio, `minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32`); each decode node automatically pulls its own half out of the packed latent. `CreateVideo` then muxes the two into a single MP4 with synced sound
- The diffusion model here is `minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors`, a different set of weights from the `fl2va` model used by the t2v/i2v templates

Ref2va's output is very sensitive to prompt wording; matching the reference tags precisely and being explicit about which reference drives which part of the shot tends to work best.

subject_definitions:
<Picture 1> is the reference for the Armored Duelist: a girl with loose dark hair, a white cinched apron over a black armored bodysuit, and one armored gauntlet. <Subject 1> (S1). (The studio backdrop is NOT referenced and is replaced by an illuminated moving subway car — she never stands on a plain background.)
<Picture 2> is the reference for the White-Haired Punk: a girl with short white hair, pink eyes, a pink bralette and polka-dot shorts, headphones and metal chains at her hips. <Subject 2> (S2). (The studio backdrop is NOT referenced and is replaced by the same moving subway car — she never stands on a plain background.)

retention_analysis:
<Picture 1> (whole sequence): fully_preserved - only the dark hair, white apron over the black armored bodysuit, and the armored gauntlet are retained; the studio backdrop is excluded and must never appear.
<Picture 2> (whole sequence): fully_preserved - only the short white hair, pink eyes, pink bralette, polka-dot shorts, headphones and hip chains are retained; the studio backdrop is excluded and must never appear.

detailed_description:
A slick cinematic action shot inside a moving subway car: stainless handrail poles, upholstered seats, a sliding partition door, windows streaking with tunnel lights, the car rocking and tilting with the track. Two different fight styles duel — S1 the cool defensive counter-fighter who reads and deflects and answers with one decisive strike, S2 the relentless forward-pressing attacker who hammers in combos and eats a hit to land her own. Every exchange is a cause-and-effect gamble: S2 commits, S1 exploits the opening or S2's pressure forces S1 onto the back foot, so the advantage swings back and forth and neither ever gets a clean lead. The two never settle into a completed move; each strike's follow-through is the wind-up of the next, attack and counter overlapping in time, so there is never a single beat where both are planted still. The camera rides them in one never-cutting dolly-crane that sways with the car, no jump cut, always slightly ahead of the action.
At 00:00.000, S2 lunges first, a 崩拳 jab probing S1's guard — S1 doesn't block, she slips the jab and, reading that S2 is thrown forward off-balance by her own lunge, answers with a 横扫 that S2 only barely rolls with by ducking under the handrail; S1's follow-through carries her shoulder low, and S2, still moving, punches a 横扫 backhand into that open shoulder, S1's body tipping into a seat back.
At 00:01.200, S1 catches the pole with the rebound, so instead of falling she turns that recoil into a rising 撩踢 aimed at the now-committed S2; S2 铁板桥 leans back off the pole letting the kick miss by a hair, and in that same bend springs a 侧空翻 over S1's shoulders, landing already circling to cut off the escape route S1 was angling for.
At 00:02.400, S2, seeing S1 slide toward the window, feints a high strike to make S1 lean back, then drops and 仆步 lunges a 扫堂腿 under S1's planted heel, sweeping her base so S1's leg goes out from under her; S1 catches the seat edge instead of falling, turning the stumble into a low guard, and S2 presses in.
At 00:03.600, the train brakes and S1 uses that lurch — she lets the forward momentum carry her into a 直进手 rammed at S2's chest, so S2, instead of dodging, angles it off her forearm; S2 grabs S1's wrist in the 缠手 and, using the braking slide, spins S1's arm down toward the seat back.
At 00:04.800, S2 wrenches S1's shoulder into the seat but S1 is already breaking free with her off hand and driving a 膝撞 up — S2 pulls back and eats only part of it, sliding off down the aisle while S1 uses the release to regain her guard.
At 00:06.000, they trade a rapid 拆招 of 双拳 across each other's guard, S2 hammering a low kick while S1 snaps a 回身掌 that catches S2's jaw; S2 takes it and immediately repays with a second 横扫 to S1's ribs, so the two land a hit each in the same beat, neither giving ground.
At 00:07.200, as the train jolts into a brake they split for a beat — S2 winds a high 回旋踢 and S1 answers a wide 横扫, the two paths cracking just short of each other; the momentum carries them apart down the car without either planting, S2 landing crouched and sliding by the far handrail, S1 skidding onto one knee by the cracked window, both already bracing and re-reading each other's next read as the frame ends.

overall_soundscape:
The train rattles, rocks and brakes with metallic screeches, poles clank, boots and feet pound and skid on the metal floor, bodies hit the seats, the window and partition with dull cracks, glass webbing with a snap, two sets of hard short breaths never stop.

non_diegetic_music:
A tight percussion-and-string drive, taiko accents on every hit, an unbroken rising ostinato, then a suspended drone over the rocking car as the two hang apart, no pause, no resolve.
